item.title: Top 5 Methods to Understand Why Pandas Merges Are Faster Than Data.Table Merges
item.description:
Introduction

When comparing the in-memory merging capabilities of the Pandas library in Python with the data.table package in R, several curious minds often wonder why Pandas appears to have the upper hand in performance. Is it due to Python’s inherent speed? Or are there specific trade-offs and optimizations at play? Furthermore, can data.table perform efficient joins without using the standard merge functions like merge(X, Y, all=FALSE) or merge(X, Y, all=TRUE)? This post delves into these questions and explores various solutions along the way.
